artifacts_produced.deploy_evidence: extract_v2(bronze_uri, body, ext): v1's document shape (via extract(), unchanged) plus, for PDF, `lines` (every line across pages: text/page/size/bold_all/bold_first/lead_prefix/n_spans) and `section_leads` ({name, page, line_index, inline_remainder}, one per line that OPENS a SECTION_NAMES member under rule 1 -- a standalone heading OR a line whose leading bold spans, colon-trimmed and upper-cased, are a known section name); for DOCX, v1's paragraphs/headings/tables are BYTE-EQUAL (the control) plus `section_leads` (one per paragraph whose text-before-the-first-colon, colon-trimmed and upper-cased, is a section name); XLSX unchanged. SECTION_NAMES is the 45-name frozenset ported verbatim from the CRO's measured set (the scan's 25 names + the PFOE author's 20), with VALUATION deliberately excluded (a pillar lead, never a section name); a name followed by a trailing number matches on its alphabetic prefix. The PDF line/lead rules (_pdf_lines_and_leads, _pdf_section_lead_name, _match_section_name) are a direct port of measure_pdf_extractability.py's pdf_lines/section_name_of, rewritten in this module (never imported from the deliverables script). --run-v2 measured live against the 123 bronze research-report objects (same walk --write uses): first run bronze_reports 123 v2_stored 123 put_performed 123 existed 0 read_failed 0, docx_control identical 25 of 25, section_leads_pdf_files_with_any 39 of 52; second (idempotent) run bronze_reports 123 v2_stored 123 put_performed 0 existed 123 read_failed 0, same docx_control/section_leads totals. --census-leads measured live: pdf_files 52 with_inline_leads 22 with_standalone_only 17 with_none 13. No v1 object was rewritten or deleted (123 extract.json objects before and after, verified by a direct list).

2 new tests added (6 total in the file, all offline under the package poison, fixtures built in code): (1) test_docx_v2_control_byte_equal_and_section_leads -- asserts extract_v2's docx paragraphs/headings/tables are == extract()'s (THE CONTROL, byte-equal in the structural sense) on the existing fixture, then on a second fixture asserts a 'Recommendation: Buy the position...' paragraph yields a section_leads entry {name: RECOMMENDATION, paragraph_index: 0, inline_remainder: '...'} and a 'Valuation: ...' paragraph yields none; (2) test_pdf_v2_inline_lead_opens_section_standalone_closes_valuation_does_not -- a PyMuPDF-built fixture with an inline bold lead ('RECOMMENDATION: <body>' on one line, bold+non-bold spans), a standalone all-bold heading ending in a colon ('RISKS AND CONSDIERATIONS:'), and a bold inline 'Valuation: <body>' line; asserts exactly 2 section_leads (RECOMMENDATION with the correct inline_remainder, and RISKS AND CONSDIERATIONS), asserts VALUATION is never a member, and asserts every `lines` entry carries the 7 spec'd fields.
